title: Shadow traffic: implement data retention + redaction pipeline for prompts/responses and identifiers
creator: Talia Benson
project: Shadow traffic tool for eval metrics
description:
Problem
Shadow traffic introduces storage of prompt/response artifacts and metadata used for asynchronous scoring and quality deltas. Without strict redaction + retention controls, we risk:
- Storing customer PII/secrets in prompt/response payloads
- Violating data minimization commitments and Dedicated/Private contractual requirements
- Creating high-cardinality identifiers that leak tenant/user info and blow up metrics/warehouse costs

This ticket implements the v1 redaction + retention mechanisms end-to-end:
- Hashing identifiers (request id, user id, conversation id where present) in a tenant-scoped way
- Prompt/response truncation and structured allowlists (store only what we need for scoring + example drilldowns)
- Configurable retention windows per deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), with sane defaults and hard caps
- Controls to disable artifact storage while still emitting aggregate scoring/quality metrics

Scope
- Shadow artifact storage layer: payload transformation, encryption, and TTL/retention enforcement
- Telemetry ingestion: ensure raw fields are never persisted unredacted; enforce schema-level drop/transform
- Console example drilldowns: ensure examples shown are post-redaction, and sampling is consistent with retention

Non-scope
- Customer-provided custom redaction code execution (v1)
- Full DSAR automation (we will not store stable raw identifiers; hashed IDs reduce DSAR surface)

Owners/partners
- Primary: Kevin Osei (Audit/SIEM & retention controls)
- Security review: Marcus Lin
- Telemetry/pipelines: Nadia Rahman / Caleb Johnson
- Product input on defaults: Marissa Cole / Paula Mendes

Background constraints
- Shadow path must be fail-open. If redaction pipeline fails, we drop artifact persistence rather than block user requests.
- Dedicated/Private must support configurable retention with auditability of config changes.
- Cardinality: prohibit storing arbitrary tags/labels and raw request headers; only allow an explicit allowlist.
acceptance_criteria:
1) No raw prompt/response text is persisted unless it has passed the redaction transform (allowlist + truncation + secret/PII scrub).
2) Identifiers written to shadow artifact storage are tenant-scoped HMACs (no reversible hashing; no shared global salt).
3) Retention enforcement:
   - Hosted default: 7 days for artifacts, 30 days for aggregates (no prompt text), 90 days for alert events.
   - Dedicated default: 7 days artifacts; configurable 1–30 days via policy; aggregates configurable up to 180 days.
   - Private default: artifacts disabled; if enabled, customer-controlled retention with documented on-disk location + purge job.
4) Ability to disable artifact storage while still computing aggregates (store scores only, plus minimal metadata).
5) Audit logs emitted for retention/redaction configuration changes (create/update shadow experiment and policy changes).
6) Backfill/cleanup job runs safely and is observable (dashboards + alerts for purge lag / deletion failures).
7) Unit + integration tests cover: truncation, allowlist behavior, HMAC determinism, retention TTL application, and fail-open dropping behavior.
8) Security sign-off from Marcus Lin documented in ticket comments with any required follow-ups tracked as separate issues.
implementation_notes:
Data model (v1)
- shadow_artifacts table/blob:
  - tenant_id (internal)
  - shadow_pair_id (UUID)
  - request_fingerprint (already privacy-reviewed deterministic fingerprint; no raw text)
  - control_variant_ref / shadow_variant_ref
  - created_at
  - redacted_request_payload (JSON stored as bytes; encrypted at rest)
  - redacted_response_payload (optional; encrypted at rest)
  - payload_schema_version
  - artifact_ttl_seconds (computed at write time)

Redaction transform
- Approach: structured allowlist + truncation + targeted scrubbing.
- Allowlist (chat):
  - messages[].role
  - messages[].content (truncated)
  - tool_calls/function_call fields: store only tool name + argument keys; drop argument values by default (configurable allowlist for select keys later)
  - system prompt: allowed, truncated; still scrubbed
- Allowlist (text completion):
  - prompt (truncated + scrubbed)
- Always drop:
  - request headers
  - raw customer identifiers (end-user IDs, emails)
  - ip addresses, user agent
  - any field not explicitly allowlisted

Truncation
- Default max_chars per field:
  - messages[].content: 2,000 chars
  - prompt: 4,000 chars
  - response text: 2,000 chars (only if examples enabled)
- Rationale: enough for rubric checks (format adherence, refusal detection, instruction following) and targeted example inspection.

Scrubbing
- Apply lightweight scrubbing to allowlisted text fields:
  - email-like patterns -> "[REDACTED_EMAIL]"
  - long digit runs / SSNs -> "[REDACTED_NUMERIC]"
  - common API key prefixes (sk-, rk-, etc.) -> "[REDACTED_SECRET]"
- Note: this is best-effort; primary protection is allowlist + truncation + short retention.

Hashed identifiers
- Use HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-scoped key:
  - hmac_key = KMS-derived per-tenant data-key (or per-deployment in Private)
  - hashed_user_id = HMAC(hmac_key, user_id)
  - hashed_conversation_id = HMAC(hmac_key, conversation_id)
- Do not persist raw user_id/conversation_id.
- Do not reuse HMAC keys across tenants.

Retention/TTL
- Compute artifact_ttl_seconds at ingestion based on resolved policy:
  - route shadow policy -> experiment policy -> tenant defaults -> deployment defaults
- Enforce via:
  - object storage lifecycle rules (Hosted/Dedicated)
  - scheduled purge worker for metadata rows (warehouse) to ensure query surfaces respect retention even if blob lifecycle lags
- Provide a "retention_disabled" mode for Private (default) where artifacts are never written.

Fail-open behavior
- If redaction transform throws or KMS key unavailable:
  - drop artifact write
  - still emit minimal shadow_pair telemetry (cardinality-safe) and scoring metadata if present
  - increment counter: shadow_artifact_write_dropped_total{reason}

Permissions & access
- Only Console roles with "Quality:ViewExamples" can query artifacts.
- Access is audited and rate-limited; examples endpoint must never return raw unredacted payload.

Observability
- Metrics:
  - shadow_artifact_write_success_total
  - shadow_artifact_write_dropped_total{reason}
  - shadow_artifact_purge_success_total / _error_total
  - shadow_artifact_purge_lag_seconds (p95)
- Logs: structured logs with shadow_pair_id, tenant_id, reason codes (no payload text).
rollout_plan:
1) Behind feature flags:
   - shadow_artifacts_write_enabled (default off)
   - shadow_artifacts_examples_enabled (default off)
2) Internal dogfood tenant:
   - enable artifacts at 3-day retention
   - enable examples for Console-only users
   - verify purge + access logs
3) Dedicated beta tenants:
   - default artifacts 7 days; examples off by default
   - opt-in examples with explicit customer acknowledgement in Console
4) GA:
   - Hosted defaults as per Acceptance Criteria
   - Publish retention/redaction docs; add an onboarding checklist item for Dedicated/Private.
testing_plan:
Unit tests
- Allowlist: unknown fields are dropped
- Truncation: content length limits enforced; UTF-8 safe truncation
- Scrubbing: representative patterns replaced
- HMAC determinism: same input -> same output; different tenant keys -> different outputs
- Fail-open: simulated KMS failure results in drop + metric increment

Integration tests
- Ingest shadow_pair event -> artifact write -> examples endpoint returns only redacted payload
- Retention: TTL applied; purge worker removes expired entries; Console queries no longer return expired artifacts
- RBAC: unauthorized roles cannot access examples endpoint

Load tests
- Verify artifact writing overhead stays within shadow path budget; validate backpressure behavior does not impact control response latency.
open_questions:
1) Should we allow storing tool argument values for a small allowlist of keys (e.g., "country", "locale")? Proposal: defer to v2; keep v1 as keys-only.
2) For streaming responses, do we store partial output for examples or only final assembled output (when available)? Current v1: store first N chars of final assembled output when stream completes; if stream truncated/aborted, store nothing.
3) Dedicated customers asking for >30 day artifact retention: product stance is no for v1 (artifacts are high-risk); allow longer retention for aggregates only.
4) Should we support customer-provided regex redaction lists in Dedicated? Proposal: defer; too much config surface + risk of false negatives.

comments: 2026-01-16 (Marcus Lin): +1 to allowlist-first. Please do not store tool arguments by value in v1; keys-only is fine. Use tenant-scoped HMAC; no global salts. Add a metric for dropped writes + reason and ensure logs never include payloads.

2026-01-22 (Logan Wright): For Dedicated, we need a documented knob and hard caps. Please keep artifacts max 30d; aggregates can be longer. Also ensure schema versioning so we can evolve allowlists without breaking old reads.

2026-02-03 (Nadia Rahman): Ingestion pipeline can compute TTL at write time, but we need policy resolution to be cheap. Suggest caching resolved retention policy per route_id for 60s. Also: warehouse table must not include raw text columns (store blob refs only).

2026-02-12 (Paula Mendes): Console should show retention settings in experiment summary and require an acknowledgement when examples are enabled. Also want a warning that example payloads are redacted + truncated and may not match full user prompt.

2026-02-20 (Kevin Osei): Implemented tenant-scoped HMAC via KMS data key derivation. Added purge worker + lifecycle rules for blobs. Examples endpoint now returns redacted payload only; added RBAC gate. Requesting security review on PR-24980.

2026-02-26 (Marcus Lin): Reviewed PR-24980. Blocking item: ensure we drop any header-derived fields before artifact write (I saw one code path that allowed request_id header passthrough). Once fixed, consider this approved for beta.
